primary_meaning: Human efforts to achieve justification, righteousness, or earn salvation through perfect obedience to God's commandments, typically characterized as legalism and contrasted with faith.

alternatives.meaning: Jewish identity and boundary markers, specifically circumcision, dietary laws, and Sabbath observance, which separated Jews from Gentiles (the New Perspective on Paul).
The ceremonial and ritual precepts of the Old Covenant which have passed away, as distinct from the moral law.
Specific sectarian halakhic rulings or legal interpretations, as seen in the Dead Sea Scrolls document 4QMMT.

notes: The interpretation of this phrase is the central debate in Pauline studies today. The traditional Protestant view sees it as a critique of legalistic works-righteousness, while the New Perspective on Paul views it as a critique of Jewish ethnocentrism and covenant boundary markers.
